statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-56390: GNU Bison accepts file paths from %output and %header directives in a grammar file and lets them override the output options given by the caller, so processing an attacker-supplied grammar can write generated files to any location the Bison process can write, overwriting existing files. Sources: https://cert.pl/en/posts/2026/07/CVE-2026-56389/ and the upstream fix https://cgit.git.savannah.gnu.org/cgit/bison.git/commit/?id=8d101c19d4d9aaedf83a448c925513742d4efcf0, which rejects a slash in %header and %output file names in src/parse-gram.y and the generated src/parse-gram.c. No GNU Bison release contains the fix yet; 3.8.2 is the latest release at https://ftp.gnu.org/gnu/bison/. We read every package built from source bison in the DHI Alpine 3.23 package repository: bison 3.8.2-r2 and 3.8.2-r3 for x86_64 and aarch64, and the bison-doc packages of both versions, which hold documentation, examples and manual pages; each package was checked against its index checksum. In all four bison packages, /usr/bin/bison, a dynamically linked program for musl, contains neither of the messages invalid %%output file name ignored and invalid %%header file name ignored that the fix adds; the same search finds the message %s failed with status %d as a control. So no published build carries the fix. A rebuild that applies the upstream fix is pending, and until it is published every published build is affected.
